quizName:
DMV Practice Test  #2
										  					
  

25 Questions • Passing Score 20

questions.question: When you see a school bus stopped with its stop arm out, you should:

options.text: Stop completely and wait before moving forward.
Honk your horn and pass on the left side.
Keep driving when you think the children have finished getting off.
Pass the bus before its door opens.

questions.correctAnswerText: Stop completely and wait before moving forward.
questions.explanation: You must come to a complete stop when you see a school bus with its stop arm out. Do not move until the stop arm goes back in.

questions.question: Alcohol causes:
questions.explanation: Even a small amount of alcohol hurts your eyesight, decision-making, focus, and coordination.

questions.question: Before driving, a driver taking over-the-counter medicine should:

options.text: Read the label on the medicine.
Drive anyway even if there are warnings.

questions.correctAnswerText: Read the label on the medicine.
questions.explanation: Many over-the-counter medicines can affect your driving. Check the label for warnings about driving. If you are unsure, ask your doctor or pharmacist if you can safely drive while taking the medicine.

questions.question: If another driver is acting aggressively toward you, you should:

options.text: Do not make eye contact, slow down, and let them pass.
Cut them off to make them slow down.
Make a rude gesture to show your disapproval.

questions.correctAnswerText: Do not make eye contact, slow down, and let them pass.
questions.explanation: Stay calm and put distance between you and the aggressive driver. Slow down and let them pass. Do not look at them and do not make rude gestures.

questions.question: A pedestrian begins to cross in front of your car. You should:

options.text: Speed up and pass in front of them.

questions.explanation: Always slow down and be ready to stop when you see pedestrians. Be extra careful around children. Always let pedestrians cross safely in a crosswalk.

questions.question: To change lanes safely, you should:

options.text: Check mirrors and signal, then change lanes.
Signal, check mirrors, check your blind spot by looking over your shoulder, then change lanes.
Signal, check mirrors, and change lanes.

questions.correctAnswerText: Signal, check mirrors, check your blind spot by looking over your shoulder, then change lanes.
questions.explanation: Turn on your signal first. Check your rearview and side mirrors. Look over your shoulder to see your blind spot and make sure no other car is moving into that lane. Only change lanes when it is safe.

questions.question: Which statement about seat belts and child restraints is true?

options.text: Never put a baby or small child in the front seat of a car with airbags.
An airbag can hurt a baby or small child, even in a minor crash.
Make sure all passengers wear a seat belt or use a child restraint.

questions.explanation: Before you drive, put on your seat belt and make sure all passengers have seat belts or child restraints. Seat belts greatly reduce your chances of being hurt or killed in a crash. Children 12 and under must sit in the back seat with proper restraints. Never put a rear-facing baby seat in the front of a car with an airbag.

questions.question: Your brake lights tell other drivers that you:
questions.explanation: Brake lights show other drivers that you are slowing down or stopping. Your brake lights must always work when you drive.

questions.question: When driving near a blind person with a white cane or guide dog, you should:

options.text: Slow down and be ready to stop.

questions.correctAnswerText: Slow down and be ready to stop.
questions.explanation: When you see a blind person with a white cane or guide dog, slow down and give them the right-of-way. Be ready to stop to keep them safe.

questions.question: This sign means:
questions.explanation: Warning signs are yellow with black markings. They alert you to road conditions and hazards ahead. This sign warns you that a traffic signal is coming. Be ready for red, yellow, or green lights and watch for crossing traffic.

questions.question: If you pass your exit on the interstate, what should you do?

options.text: Quickly cut across traffic to make your turn.
Make a U-turn to go back to the exit.
Continue driving and use the next exit.
Put your vehicle in reverse to go back to the exit.

questions.correctAnswerText: Continue driving and use the next exit.
questions.explanation: Do not make a sudden turn or U-turn to catch your exit. Keep driving safely to the next exit.

questions.question: Who must wear a seat belt?
questions.explanation: All drivers and front seat passengers must wear seat belts. Children under 18 must use seat belts or car seats in any seat.

questions.question: Before changing lanes on a multilane highway, you should:

options.text: Check your mirrors and blind spots.

questions.correctAnswerText: Check your mirrors and blind spots.
questions.explanation: Look in your rearview and side mirrors. Also look over your shoulder to check your blind spot before changing lanes.

questions.question: If you miss your exit on an interstate expressway, what should you do?

options.text: Get off at the next exit and come back to the exit you missed.
Roll down your window and ask the driver next to you for help.

questions.correctAnswerText: Get off at the next exit and come back to the exit you missed.
questions.explanation: Never back up or turn around on the highway. Drive safely to the next exit and turn around there.

questions.question: When is it important to slow down?

options.text: When the road is wet or slippery.

questions.explanation: Slow down on narrow or winding roads, at intersections, at railroad crossings, on hills, in sharp curves, near pedestrians, and when roads are wet or slippery.

questions.question: How can you reduce road rage and aggressive driving?
questions.explanation: To prevent road rage, use turn signals, follow speed limits, and leave plenty of time for your trip.

questions.question: If someone is driving aggressively behind you, you should:

options.text: Try to get out of the aggressive driver's way.
Stare at the driver as he or she is passing you.
Speed up as he or she is passing you.

questions.correctAnswerText: Try to get out of the aggressive driver's way.
questions.explanation: Get out of the way of an aggressive driver. Do not make eye contact or challenge them. Speeding up or blocking them will only make things worse.

questions.question: Why shouldn't you follow other cars too closely?

options.text: You may not see the road between the cars.
You may not have time to stop if the vehicle in front of you slows or stops suddenly.
You may not see the vehicle's turn signals.
You may not see the other vehicle's brake lights.

questions.correctAnswerText: You may not have time to stop if the vehicle in front of you slows or stops suddenly.
questions.explanation: If you follow too closely and the car ahead slows down suddenly, you may not have enough time to stop and avoid a crash.

questions.question: What is the speed limit in a school zone unless otherwise posted?
questions.explanation: The speed limit in a school zone is 20 miles per hour unless a different speed is posted. Always drive carefully in school zones.

questions.question: What does this sign mean?

options.text: Highway changes ahead and to the right.
Hiking trails ahead and to the right.
Hotel ahead and to the right.
Hospital ahead and to the right.

questions.correctAnswerText: Hospital ahead and to the right.
questions.explanation: This sign shows that hospital emergency services are located to the right.

questions.question: When should you look over your shoulder to check your blind spot?

options.text: When pulling toward or away from a curb.

questions.explanation: Check your blind spot every time you move your vehicle. This includes turning, changing lanes, and pulling toward or away from a curb.

questions.question: When driving, you must stop your vehicle:

options.text: When a traffic officer orders you to stop.

questions.explanation: You must stop at stop signs, red lights, and whenever a traffic officer tells you to stop.

questions.question: This road sign means:
questions.explanation: This sign warns that a steep downhill grade is ahead.

questions.question: To drive safely at night, you should:

options.text: Keep a greater distance between your car and the car ahead.
Not drive if you are tired.
Make sure your headlights work properly.

questions.explanation: Night driving is harder because you cannot see as well. Take these steps to stay safe and protect other drivers.

questions.question: If a traffic officer is directing traffic at a working traffic light, drivers should:

options.text: Follow what the traffic light shows.
Watch what the other cars are doing.

questions.explanation: When a traffic officer is directing traffic, follow their directions instead of the traffic light.
